summaryAssertions.text: Use the manufacturing application as the initial integrated AI-development trial. Rationale: It provides a controlled MVP-adjacent environment to validate tooling, requirements quality and workflow integration.
Introduce AI-based code review, with failed checks ultimately blocking artifact generation. Rationale: Improve code quality and ensure issues are surfaced and resolved consistently.

Retain functional testing within 360/full-stack teams while Gaurav remains responsible for integration and regression testing. Rationale: Reflects current specialist ownership, though it requires active bottleneck management.

Treat small changes through a lightweight service-project route and major strategic initiatives through NPI governance in principle. Rationale: Apply proportionate control while avoiding unnecessary process for minor work.
Theo retains strategic UI/UX guidance while Mandar/team may take greater execution ownership. Rationale: Reduce operational design dependency without losing framework and UX consistency.

Develop a proposed multi-month resource forecasting and planning model with Mandar and relevant stakeholders. Owner: Peter. Deadline: To be defined.
Reflect on the lightweight-versus-NPI product intake proposal and revisit with Peter. Owner: Mandar. Deadline: To be defined.
Share AI-powered product-design course learnings, scope and practical organisational applications. Owner: Mandar. Deadline: As course progresses.

topics.summary: All four OGT trainees have transitioned into regular development work and are contributing effectively. Munishka has joined the ML testing area, but recruitment for testing roles remains difficult because candidates are not passing later technical assessment stages. V&V, integration and regression testing become constrained when Gaurav is allocated to firmware work, delaying 360 testing.

"Functional testing is supported by the 360/full-stack teams."
"Gaurav retains integration and regression testing responsibilities."
"Gaurav's firmware workload can delay 360 testing."

topics.summary: Peter has not yet completed previously discussed employee cases because of competing priorities and committed to resolve them during the week. He also clarified that redundancies referenced in Toby's email are limited to sales and marketing and do not affect R&D. The reorganisation is intended to reduce cold-calling and management overhead, increase marketing automation and lead quality, and concentrate sales effort on higher-probability opportunities.

"The redundancy communication originated from Toby's email."
"The reorganisation is limited to sales and marketing."
"R&D is not affected by the restructuring."
"Some sales roles are redundant."
"New sales or business-development roles may be created."

decisions.text: Position the sales and marketing changes as a strategic redesign rather than a cost-saving exercise. (Rationale: The intended model reduces low-value activity and strengthens qualified-lead generation and opportunity focus.)

actions.text: Complete the outstanding employee cases and provide an update. (Owner: Peter, Deadline: During the week)

risks.text: "Unresolved employee cases may create avoidable people-management risk."
"Team concerns may persist if the scope and rationale for redundancies are not clearly communicated."
"The commercial redesign may create short-term coverage gaps while roles are removed or added."

topics.summary: AI is positioned as a productivity lever intended to avoid unnecessary future hiring rather than replace R&D employees. Developers currently use Copilot and Claude primarily for prompted code snippets and manual adaptation. The manufacturing application is serving as the first integrated Rodeo/Roo Code trial, with Shweta preparing the environment, structured requirements and tool integrations.

keyFacts.text: "Developers currently use Copilot and Claude."
"Current AI use is mainly prompted code generation followed by manual adaptation."
"The manufacturing app is the initial integrated Rodeo/Roo Code development trial."
"Shweta is setting up the AI-development environment."
"AI code-review warnings and issues are intended to be shared and resolved regularly."
"Failed code-review checks should block artifact generation."
"The approach will be trialled alongside the MVP and fully implemented after the MVP."

decisions.text: Introduce AI-based code review into the development pipeline. (Rationale: To improve code quality discipline and ensure unresolved failed checks prevent artifact generation.)

Use the manufacturing-app MVP as the initial integrated AI-development trial. (Rationale: The trial provides a controlled product context for validating tooling, requirements discipline and workflow integration.)

actions.text: Set up the integrated AI-development environment, including well-defined stories, requirements and tool linkage. (Owner: Shweta, Deadline: During MVP trial)
Keep Peter updated on AI-development and code-review progress. (Owner: Mandar, Deadline: Ongoing)

risks.text: "Current AI usage is not yet integrated into standard development workflows."
"Poorly defined stories or requirements could limit the effectiveness of AI-assisted development."
"Code-review enforcement may affect delivery flow if warning triage and remediation are not operationalised."

topics.summary: Mandar has initiated an R&D page to centralise documentation that is currently dispersed and to establish a monthly delivery dashboard. The dashboard is intended to report delivery status, pace, gaps, blockers and improvement opportunities. Peter challenged the number of blocked issues, and Mandar clarified that blocked epics should be the primary leadership concern because many blocked stories and tasks reflect dependencies, unavailable inputs or deprioritisation rather than unresolved technical blockage.

keyFacts.text: "Mandar has started an R&D documentation page."
"The planned dashboard will be produced monthly."
"Dashboard coverage includes delivery status, pace, gaps, blockers and improvement areas."
"Most blocked items are firmware-related."
"Some blocked items relate to branding."
"A comments/response column has been added for supporting information."
"Team members have been asked to populate supporting information."

decisions.text: Focus leadership attention primarily on blocked epics rather than all blocked stories and tasks. (Rationale: Many lower-level blocked items are controlled dependencies, unavailable inputs or work excluded from the current release.)

actions.text: Populate dashboard comments and supporting information for blocked items. (Owner: R&D team members, Deadline: Unknown)
Continue developing the central R&D page and monthly dashboard. (Owner: Mandar, Deadline: Monthly)

risks.text: "Inconsistent use of 'blocked' can overstate delivery risk and reduce management confidence in reporting."
"Firmware and branding dependencies may become material if they are not actively resolved."
"Incomplete comments may prevent leaders from distinguishing controlled dependencies from critical blockers."

topics.summary: Peter requested a forward-looking workload and backlog view by team and discipline to identify emerging bottlenecks and balance prioritised work. Mandar demonstrated existing Jira views for team backlogs, Kanban status, plan/calendar and individual assignee capacity. However, the current way of working and maturity of assignment data do not provide a reliable multi-month resource forecast, and creating one would require a broader planning-model change.

keyFacts.text: "Peter requested a forward-looking workload and backlog view by team and discipline."
"Jira currently provides team backlog, Kanban status, plan/calendar and individual assignee-capacity views."
"Current tooling does not provide a reliable multi-month resource forecast."
"Peter suggested a planning horizon of approximately three months."
"The aim is to avoid assigning further work to fully allocated teams while prioritising work for less constrained teams."

actions.text: Develop the proposed forward-planning model and involve Mandar and other stakeholders. (Owner: Peter, Deadline: Unknown)

risks.text: "Work may be prioritised into already constrained disciplines while capacity exists elsewhere."
"Future bottlenecks may be identified too late for effective rebalancing."
"A forecast based on immature assignment data could create false confidence."

topics.summary: Peter proposed separate delivery paths based on the scale and strategic impact of incoming work. Small enhancements, bugs, change requests and individual features would enter through a service project for triage and lightweight prioritisation. Major new capabilities or product-changing initiatives would proceed through NPI governance, including feasibility, planning, stakeholder-impact assessment, marketing and support preparation, and project-board review.

keyFacts.text: "Small enhancements, bugs, change requests and individual features would use the service project."
"Larger strategic or product-changing initiatives would use NPI governance."
"A small new activity or function within an existing product was cited as a lightweight example."
"Visualizer/Wiscom Learn-type concepts were cited as NPI-level examples."
"The proposal aims to avoid excessive project-board involvement in minor work."

actions.text: Reflect on the proposed two-path intake model and revisit it with Peter. (Owner: Mandar, Deadline: Unknown)

risks.text: "Unclear thresholds could lead to inconsistent routing of work between service and NPI paths."
"Over-governance of minor changes could slow responsiveness."
"Under-governance of strategic initiatives could leave stakeholder, marketing, support and feasibility impacts unmanaged."

topics.summary: Peter advocated an agile mindset rather than rigid methodology: requirements should be sufficiently clear for R&D to execute without prolonged approval cycles, while core concepts are settled before development. Mandar is exploring whether he and the team can take on more UI/UX execution, supported by an AI-powered product-design course. Peter supported this direction in principle, with Theo retaining responsibility for high-level UX intent, guidelines and product requirements.

keyFacts.text: "Peter emphasised an agile mindset rather than strict agile methodology."
"Mandar should oversee technical, backend and database coherence."
"Theo should provide UI/UX oversight and guidelines."
"Mandar is undertaking an IIMK course on AI-powered product design."
"Existing product and UI frameworks are considered more mature than in early project stages."
"The delegation must not create unsustainable workload for Mandar."

decisions.text: Support a model in which Theo defines high-level UX intent, guidelines and product requirements while Mandar and the team execute within the established framework. (Rationale: This should reduce operational load on Theo and avoid repeated design reviews while retaining quality and coherence.)

actions.text: Share relevant AI-powered product-design learnings, scope and practical organisational ideas as the course progresses. (Owner: Mandar, Deadline: Ongoing)

risks.text: "Insufficiently clear requirements could create R&D rework and excessive back-and-forth."
"Unclear UI/UX review thresholds could weaken consistency or reintroduce approval delays."
"Additional UI/UX execution responsibility could overload Mandar."

topics.summary: Peter wants R&D involved earlier in major or uncertain initiatives to provide feasibility input, concept validation and potentially quick mockups or proofs of concept before requirements are finalised. The intended flow is concept, collaborative POC or feasibility review, final requirements and acceptance criteria, then normal planning and development. Mandar warned that informal POC work could disrupt workflows, release planning and project clarity; no final operating process was agreed.

keyFacts.text: "Peter proposed early R&D involvement before final requirements for major or uncertain initiatives."
"The proposed flow is concept, collaborative POC/feasibility review, final requirements and acceptance criteria, then normal delivery planning."
"Mandar identified risks to R&D workflow, release planning and project clarity from informal POC work."
"A possible option is to route POCs through normal planning and Mangesh using a dedicated POC tag."
"Peter suggested preserving approximately 10% capacity for rapid prototyping and concept exploration."
"September is fully booked for Peter; he is considering an India visit in early October."

decisions.text: Do not prescribe a final POC process until governance, ownership and planning integration have been further designed. (Rationale: The process must enable rapid validation without undermining committed release work or creating uncontrolled activity.)

actions.text: Continue discussion and develop a process for POC governance, ownership and integration with normal planning. (Owner: Peter and Mandar, Deadline: Unknown)
Consider whether POC work can be routed through normal planning with a dedicated POC tag. (Owner: Mandar and Mangesh, Deadline: Unknown)

risks.text: "Uncontrolled POC activity could disrupt planned R&D work and committed releases."
"Requirements may continue to change during development if feasibility validation occurs too late."
"Reserved prototype capacity could become untracked or confused with normal delivery work."
"Unresolved linkage between POCs and roadmap commitments may create delivery ambiguity."
